- **Postponing a task with a non-whole-minute due date:** the result is rounded down, so it can move by slightly less than the requested hours. The test covers this.

due date rounding whole minute.value: Per tech lead Maya: any due date written by NEW code/commands must be rounded down to a whole minute (stored due_at is a multiple of 60, still a Unix timestamp in seconds). Existing create_task and `add` command are exempt and must not change (sync service relies on their exact-second behaviour).

`postpone ID HOURS` CLI + api.postpone_task(task_id, hours) -> Task|None. New due_at = floor((due_at + hours*3600)/60)*60, per the whole-minute rule. `quick-add TITLE` (api.quick_add_task) sets due_at = floor((now + 86400)/60)*60. create_task and `add` untouched. Implemented on branch feat-b (commit d78ff35), pending review.

`snooze ID MINUTES` CLI + api.snooze_task(task_id, minutes) -> Task|None. New due_at = floor((due_at + minutes*60)/60)*60, following the whole-minute rule. Implemented on branch feat-a, pending review.

get_overdue_tasks() in tinytasks/api.py is deprecated and slated for removal. New code must not call it; use tinytasks.queries.tasks_due_before(cutoff) instead (cutoff = the current Unix time in seconds). The existing `overdue` command keeps using it until it is migrated.

`status` CLI (no args) prints "<N> tasks, <M> overdue": N = len(load_all()), M = len(tasks_due_before(now)). Uses tasks_due_before, not the deprecated get_overdue_tasks. Implemented on branch feat-b (commit 38ad7fb), pending review.
